title: Onyx Terminal — Trading-Floor Command
description: A Bloomberg-terminal-faithful briefing layout pairing a dense monospaced data table across two-thirds of the canvas with a fixed commentary column — crowned by a live-style ticker header and a system-status footer. Zero ornamentation; maximum information density.
philosophy: This template exists because financial professionals are exhausted by slide decks that aestheticise data at the cost of legibility. It borrows the visual grammar of the Bloomberg terminal — monospace grids, amber-on-black type, status bars — and refuses any mark that does not carry information. The layout is governed by column alignment and contrast ratio, not by brand polish. It is built for the trading desk, the risk morning brief, and the quant review room, never the keynote stage.
goodFor: Dense equity-screener, P&L, or order-book tabular data
Internal trading-desk and risk-management morning briefings
Quantitative strategy and factor-model review sessions
Live-data simulation walkthroughs for financial training
avoidFor: Consumer-facing investor storytelling or Series-A pitch decks
Image-heavy or media-rich narrative slide sequences
Brand campaign or go-to-market marketing presentations
Executive keynotes that require emotional arc or whitespace
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a financial terminal session initializing — austere, purposeful, and faintly electrified. High-contrast warm type burns against a near-black field, the title reading less like a headline and more like a system prompt awaiting confirmation. Compositional rhythm is left-anchored and strictly linear, with structural bands top and bottom enforcing a command-line formality rather than compositional drama. Avoid all softness, gradients, or decorative flourishes — every mark must earn its place by carrying information or reinforcing structure.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with full-bleed, edge-to-edge dark canvas; a fixed ticker band spans all columns at the very top and a system-status bar anchors the bottom edge. Title text block occupies columns 1–8, vertically centered in the open canvas between the two structural bands, left-aligned to the column gutter. Subtitle appears one grid row beneath the title as a secondary label field within the same left column zone. A session identifier or deck code sits flush-right inside the ticker band; no element exists outside these structural regions.

examples.promptCore: The slide must feel like a live risk-desk terminal readout captured mid-session: relentless information density, zero atmospheric whitespace, every zone justified by the data it carries. Visual tension between the wide tabular mass on the left and the narrow interpretive sidebar on the right evokes the dual-monitor rhythm of a trading workstation. Avoid softness, gradients, rounded forms, or any mark that does not carry information — even negative space should read as structural breathing between data rows, never as decorative rest. The overall mood is function-first severity: machine-precise, quietly authoritative, and deliberately anti-aesthetic.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid divides into a primary data panel spanning cols 1–8 and a commentary sidebar in cols 9–12, the two zones separated by a single vertical hairline rule with near-zero outer horizontal padding — edge-to-edge bleed reinforcing the terminal-display character. The data panel holds a monospaced tabular grid of tightly packed rows, with hierarchy enforced exclusively through column alignment and horizontal hairline row separators — no size scaling, no decorative weight. The commentary sidebar stacks discrete annotation blocks (label line above value line) as a fixed-width interpretive column. A full-bleed ticker header band (~5% canvas height) crowns the layout; a system-status footer bar of matching height anchors the bottom, both spanning all 12 columns.
